messages.author: 3fd1658253193f6a
messages.subject: problems uploading ggplots2
parts:
I'm very (very) new to R, and am currently working through a textbook to get a bit of a handle on it prior to attending a 'R' course. The textbook I'm using has recommended downloading the 'ggplots2' package for use to produce graphs. The package seems to have downloaded OK, but then when I try and activate the package it then says that there was an installation problem... any thoughts? The textbook I'm working from is from 2012, so I'm wondering whether the package is just a bit outdated and I'd be better off using something else?

Thanks in advance!

Emma

messages.author: 463b8c05680be401
messages.subject: Re: problems uploading ggplots2
parts:
Dear Emma,

there’s a first time for everything, also for asking for questions.

While the question you have might be clear for you, for me (and likely others) it is a bit of a mystery how we can help you. You should always provide clear and concise information (e.g. what error message did you get?, what did you type, on what kind of machine are you  working, are you working directly in R or are you using it from a such as Rstudio?). ggplot2 is among the most often used packages for graphs, so whenever you find a ‘mistake’ most of the time, the mistake is on your part (at least that is about my rate of mistakes to bugs).

So could you please run the following:

sessionInfo()
install.packages("ggplot2")
library("ggplot2")
sessionInfo()

and paste the output along with a more clearly defined question?

Best wishes,

Richard

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: problems uploading ggplots2
parts:
ggplot2 (not _not_ ggplot_s_2) is well maintained and probably most widely used R package out there (even Python community is translating it). Check that you have current R version and that you install it using

install.packages("ggplot2")

Once you do that, it should load fine using library(ggplot2).

Cheers,
Roman
